title: Exit-mode ontology and incident navigation board for inference services
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Problem: We lack a concise, machine-readable mapping of inference "exit modes" (the ways requests terminate) surfaced in our Console and runbook UIs. Engineers currently cross-reference traces, raw logs, HTTP/gRPC codes, and model client errors to triage. This causes slow incident response and inconsistent SLO attribution.

Goal: Create an exit-mode ontology that classifies request outcomes into a compact set of canonical categories (e.g., client-cancelled, upstream-timeout, server-overload, model-internal-error, model-reject, invalid-input, transport-error, success-with-warnings) and build an interactive incident navigation board that lets oncall and devs pivot from a noisy incident list to precise drilldowns by route, model, region, and recent rollout. The ontology must be usable by the tracing hook enrichment pipeline and the Console dashboards.
acceptance_criteria: A canonical list of exit modes published in Confluence and encoded as enums used by tracehook enrichment
Tracing hooks annotate 95% of incoming inference requests with an exit_mode tag (or 'unknown' fallback) in staging
Console incident navboard shows a heatmap of exit_mode x route with filters for model, region, and commit, and updating within 30s of traces arriving
SLO impact panel calculates token-weighted error rates per exit_mode and links to a prescriptive runbook for top three modes
A migration plan for historical telemetry to map legacy error codes to the new ontology (at least 60 days of backfilled mappings)
tasks: Draft ontology and enumeration (first-pass) and circulate to runtime, infra, and platform-sre
Implement tracehook enrichment: map gRPC/HTTP status, timeout signals, KV cache misses, model client exceptions to exit_mode tags
Update ingestion pipeline to persist exit_mode as a top-level metric and in logs for OLAP queries
Build Console navboard UI prototype (heatmap + ranked checklist + runbook links) and wire to staging metrics
Run migration job to backfill exit_mode on 30 days of historical traces and validate accuracy with sampling
Document runbooks and create paging rules for high-severity exit_modes
progress_updates: 2026-03-05: Kickoff meeting with runtime and SRE teams. Agreed on scope and success criteria; Diego assigned as owner.

2026-03-07: First-pass ontology draft completed. Initial categories: success, client_cancel, transport_error, http_4xx_user_input, http_5xx_transport, grpc_deadline, server_overload, model_error_reject, model_internal_error, cache_miss_fallback, unknown.
2026-03-09: Tracehook prototype implemented in staging runtime (adds exit_mode tag). Implemented mapping for HTTP codes and gRPC codes. Needs model-client hooks for model_* categories.
2026-03-11: Console prototype wireframe reviewed by PM and Design. Feedback: add token-weighted error rate and quick link to commit/rollout.
2026-03-13: End-to-end metric flow validated for HTTP and gRPC-originated exits in staging. Backfill plan drafted; estimate for backfill job is 2 engineering days.
comments: PM Review (Sofia Patel) 2026-03-08: Please ensure the ontology distinguishes user-caused 4xx from upstream transport issues. We need clear SLO attribution for user errors.

Runtime Lead (Mateo Ruiz) 2026-03-10: Kernel scheduling overload and autoscale-induced queue-drops show up as 'server_overload' — recommend also tagging 'backpressure' with queue_depth metrics so we can separate steady-state overload vs cold-start spikes.
Design (Lina Park) 2026-03-11: Navboard should let users pivot from an exit_mode cell to a time-series of sample traces and the most common commit hashes aligned to that spike.

Platform SRE (Ethan Nguyen) 2026-03-12: For paging rules, treat 'grpc_deadline' and 'server_overload' differently: overload should generate warnings first, deadline should trigger PagerDuty after sustained 3-minute window above threshold.
Security (Anika Rao) 2026-03-13: Note that runbooks and traces may contain PII; ensure trace sampling and redaction rules are applied before runbook links are surfaced to non-admins.
notes_and_tradeoffs: Trade-offs considered: 1) We can either keep a large, very granular set of exit modes (good for deep forensic analysis) or a compact set (better for UI clarity and SLO math). We chose a compact core set with tags/labels for optional subcategories. 2) Enriching traces at the runtime layer yields higher fidelity but requires small runtime overhead; we limit high-cardinality metadata and sample full traces to keep costs bounded. 3) Backfilling historical data is resource-heavy; prioritize 30 days and expand on demand.
next_steps: Finish model-client instrumentation for model_internal_error and model_reject (Diego)
Implement queue_depth backpressure metric and wire to navboard (Mateo)
Finalize runbook drafts and paging thresholds with SRE (Ethan)
Merge tracehook PR and run staging rollout, monitor CPU overhead for 72 hours
Schedule design follow-up to refine heatmap interactions
